screen1-a1.where: top row, far left: little Spanish flag with a 1
screen1-a1.expectation: Opens something about my Spanish course, maybe lets me switch course. The 1 might be my level.
screen1-a1.cue: The flag. The 1 means nothing to me.

first_pass.why: The flag says Spanish, fine, but the 1 is a mystery number and nothing says 'switch course'.
first_pass.solution: Put a tiny down-arrow next to the flag so I know it opens a list, and a word under the number.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing it shows what it is for and what the number means
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the flag at the top-left once. Look at what opens. Then press the phone's Back button.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens does not make plain what the flag was for, or still leaves the number unexplained
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens plainly shows what the flag is for and what the number counts
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the flag at the top left. A panel dropped down showing my Spanish course with a blue outline, a '+ Course' tile, a bar from 1 to 2 and 'Your Spanish Score is 1' with MORE ABOUT SCORE. Then New Courses: Math, Music, Chess. Back closed it.

screen1-a1.closing_comment: The flag is 'my course', and the panel spells out that the 1 is my Spanish Score. One tap and I understood both, and I'd remember it.

screen1-a2.where: top row, second: grey flame with a 1
screen1-a2.expectation: Shows my streak - how many days in a row I've practised.
screen1-a2.cue: The flame. Every habit app uses a flame for a streak.

first_pass.why: Flame plus a number is a streak. I got it in a second.

screen1-a3.where: top row, middle: blue gem with 520
screen1-a3.expectation: Shows my gems and probably opens the shop.
screen1-a3.cue: The gem picture and the big number.

first_pass.why: Gems equal game money; tapping money usually takes you to where you spend it. Good enough for me.

screen1-a4.where: top row, right: pink lightning bolt with 25
screen1-a4.expectation: Shows some kind of energy I use up doing lessons, and opens a place to refill it.
screen1-a4.cue: The lightning bolt looks like a battery / energy.

first_pass.why: I get 'energy' from the bolt, but I have no idea what uses it or what 25 means until I tap it.
first_pass.solution: A short word like 'Energy' next to it, or a 25/25 so I can see it's a full tank.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing it shows it is an app thing (not the phone battery) and what the number is
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the pink bolt-and-battery at the top-right. Read what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens still leaves you unsure what it is or what the number means
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens makes plain what it is and what the number means
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the pink bolt at the top right. An 'Energy' page opened with a pink bar reading 25 / 25 and ways to get more energy (Super, Recharge, Widget Boost, +5 energy). I closed it with the X. I finished it.

screen1-a4.closing_comment: It's clearly the app's energy, not my phone battery, and 25/25 tells me I'm full. What it still never says is what uses the energy up, so I only half understand it.

screen1-a5.where: big green banner: SECTION 1, UNIT 1 - Order at a cafe
screen1-a5.expectation: Tells me about the unit I'm on, maybe opens details or lets me jump to it.
screen1-a5.cue: The words Section 1, Unit 1, Order at a cafe.

first_pass.why: The words say where I am, great, but it looks like a heading, not a button. I wouldn't know tapping it does anything.
first_pass.solution: Add a small arrow or 'See unit' on it so I know it's pressable.

test_cases.targets: whether you can tell it can be pressed, and whether pressing it does what you expected
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the words on the green bar at the top (not the small notebook at its right end). See what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: nothing on the bar told you it could be pressed, or what opened was not what you expected from the words
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opened is what you expected from the words on the bar
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the words 'Order at a café' on the green bar. After a few seconds a page called 'Spanish Course' opened, showing big cards for Section 1, Section 2 and Section 3 with JUMP HERE on the later ones. I closed it with the X and was back on the path. I finished it.

screen1-a5.closing_comment: What opened (a map of the whole course) is roughly what I'd expect from a 'Section 1, Unit 1' banner. But nothing on the bar itself told me it was a button; I only found out by poking it.

screen1-a6.where: right end of the green banner: white notebook-with-lines icon
screen1-a6.expectation: Opens notes or a guidebook for this unit - tips and key phrases.
screen1-a6.cue: It looks like a notepad with a list.

first_pass.why: A notebook could be notes, a list, a menu. I'd have to tap it to find out.
first_pass.solution: A one-word label like 'Guide' under it.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the notebook settles which of your guesses it is
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the small notebook at the right end of the green bar. Read what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is not what you guessed, or still does not tell you what the notebook stands for
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens matches one of your guesses and you would remember it next time
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the small notebook on the right of the green bar. A page opened with the owl, 'SECTION 1, UNIT 1 - Order at a café' and KEY PHRASES: Spanish sentences with English under each and a speaker icon to hear them. I closed it with the X.

screen1-a6.closing_comment: It's the guide with key phrases for the unit, exactly one of my guesses, and I'd remember it next time. I'd still like the word 'Guide' under it, but it didn't trip me.

screen1-a7.where: under the banner on the left: green owl face with a black-and-yellow skull badge and a red ! dot
screen1-a7.expectation: No idea - some promotion or event with another game? The red ! makes me feel I have to press it.
screen1-a7.cue: The skull badge (looks like a game logo) and the red exclamation mark.

first_pass.why: It's a mash of owl, skull logo and a red alarm dot with no words. It grabs my eye away from my lesson and doesn't tell me what it is.
first_pass.solution: Tell me in words what it is ('Brawl Stars event') and lose the alarm dot unless something is actually urgent.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the badge tells you what it is and what the red mark was about
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the cartoon owl-and-skull picture at the left, under the green bar. Read what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left, or the lower blue text button if there is no X. Do NOT press any button that says it claims on or opens another game.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens still does not make plain what this is, or it takes you somewhere you could not have predicted
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens makes plain what it is and you could predict it next time
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the owl-and-skull picture. A purple 'Brawl Stars Quest' screen said 'You got Chaos Drops! Earn more rewards tomorrow.' with CLAIM ON BRAWL STARS and CLAIM LATER. I pressed CLAIM LATER, which then opened a second page, 'Brawl Stars Quest - INCOMPLETE', with a Day 1 to Day 7 list of rewards. I closed that with the X. Back on the path, the red ! had gone.

screen1-a7.closing_comment: Now I know it's a 7-day tie-in with another game, and the red ! meant a reward waiting. But 'Chaos Drops' means nothing to me, CLAIM LATER sent me into another page I didn't expect, and the whole thing pulled me away from my lesson for two screens.

screen1-a8.where: top of the winding path: round green button with a white star in a green ring
screen1-a8.cue: It's the one bright green button on the path, with a ring around it - that's 'you are here'.

first_pass.why: The colour and ring make it the obvious next step. Exactly what I want: one clear thing to press.

screen1-a9.where: purple pill under the owl: '13 days'
screen1-a9.expectation: Shows how long an event lasts or how many days are left; tapping probably opens the same thing as the owl badge.

first_pass.why: 13 days of what? Left? Done? It's a number with no subject.
first_pass.solution: Say '13 days left' plus what it's for.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the pill tells you what the time count refers to
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the purple pill under the owl-and-skull picture. Read what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens does not tell you what the days referred to
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens says plainly what the days count
test_cases.what_happened: On my phone the purple pill said 'Ended', not a number of days. I pressed it and got the same 'Brawl Stars Quest - INCOMPLETE' page with Day 1 to Day 7. I closed it with the X.

screen1-a9.closing_comment: The pill says 'Ended' while the page says 'Incomplete' and talks about days 1 to 7. Nothing tells me what the day count on the pill was counting or what has ended. I'm more confused, not less.

screen1-a11.where: path, second button: round grey star button
screen1-a11.expectation: A lesson I haven't unlocked yet - pressing probably tells me it's locked.
screen1-a11.cue: It's grey, like the others further down, and the green one is above it.

first_pass.why: Grey means 'not yet' - I get it from the path order.

screen1-a12.where: path, grey star button on the left
screen1-a12.expectation: Same as the other grey star - a later lesson, locked for now.
screen1-a12.cue: Grey colour and its place on the path.

first_pass.why: Same pattern as the grey stars around it.

screen1-a13.expectation: A reward chest I can open once I've done enough lessons.
screen1-a13.cue: A chest in a game means a prize. Grey means not ready yet.

first_pass.why: Chest equals prize, pretty universal.
Same as the other grey stars.

screen1-a15.where: bottom row, fifth: colourful blue-green bird/fish shape
screen1-a15.expectation: No idea. Maybe a video or AI chat feature?
screen1-a15.cue: Nothing - it's just a colourful blob of a creature.

first_pass.why: There's no word and the picture doesn't mean anything to me. I'd have to tap it just to find out, and then I'd lose my place.
first_pass.solution: Put a word under every bottom button, like most apps do.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the bird makes plain what it is for
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the bird in the bottom row. Read what opens (do NOT press any 'try' or subscription button). Then press the house at the left of the bottom row.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is not something you could have guessed from the bird
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens is what you expected and you would recognise the bird next time
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the colourful bird in the bottom row. A 'Subscription' page opened: 'Compare plans', Super, Super Family and Lite, each with TRY FOR $0.00. I didn't press anything on it and went back with the house.

screen1-a15.closing_comment: A bird that opens a paid-plans page. I could never have guessed that, and it sits in the main menu next to Home like any other part of the app. Now I know, I'd avoid it.

screen1-a16.where: bottom row, far left: little house (highlighted blue)
screen1-a16.expectation: Home - takes me to this main learning path.
screen1-a16.cue: House picture, and it's highlighted because I'm on it.

first_pass.why: House is home, everywhere.

screen1-a17.where: bottom row, second: orange square frame with a keyhole in the middle
screen1-a17.expectation: Maybe rewards or a treasure box? Not sure.
screen1-a17.cue: It looks a bit like a chest or a safe.

first_pass.why: It could be chests, shop, rewards... the picture is too vague to be sure.
first_pass.solution: A word under it.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the bottom-row chest settles what it stands for
test_cases.action: Press the chest in the bottom row. Read what opens. Then press the house at the left of the bottom row.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is not what the chest led you to expect
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens matches what the chest led you to expect
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the orange chest in the bottom row. A 'Quests' page opened: 'Complete quests to earn rewards!', a Friends Quest (Follow your first friend), and Daily Quests with chests as prizes. Then the cup (next try).

screen1-a17.closing_comment: Close to my 'rewards' guess, since the chests are prizes, but I'd never have come up with 'Quests'. I'll remember it now, though.

screen1-a18.where: bottom row, third: brown cup / trophy

first_pass.why: Trophy is either rankings or badges - I'd guess, not know.
first_pass.solution: A word under it.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing it settles which of your readings is right
test_cases.action: Press the cup/trophy shape in the bottom row. Read what opens. Then press the house.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is not what you expected, or you still could not tell which it would be next time
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens matches what you expected
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the brown cup. A page opened with a 1-2-3 ranking picture and 'Finish 2 lessons to start competing on Leaderboards!'.

screen1-a18.closing_comment: Leaderboard was my first guess, and the page confirmed it straight away.

screen1-a19.where: bottom row, fourth: pink speech bubble with a heart

first_pass.why: Heart plus bubble could be messages, favourites or a friends feed. Too many options.
first_pass.solution: A word under it.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing it settles which of your readings is right
test_cases.action: Press the heart-in-a-bubble in the bottom row. Read what opens. Then press the house.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is none of the things you guessed, or you could not tell which in advance
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens is what you expected
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the pink heart-in-a-bubble. A 'Feed' page opened with empty friend circles, 'Start Friend Streaks to send and receive daily gifts!', ADD FRIENDS, and a post from someone who 'shared a sentence'. Then I went to the chest (next try).

screen1-a19.closing_comment: It's the friends feed, one of my three guesses, so it wasn't a shock. But I couldn't have picked which one in advance. A word under it would settle it.

screen1-a20.where: bottom row, far right: purple bubble with three dots and a red dot
screen1-a20.expectation: More options / everything else, or maybe chat. The red dot says something new is waiting.
screen1-a20.cue: Three dots usually means 'more'; the red dot means a notification.

first_pass.why: Three dots is 'more', OK, but in a speech bubble it also looks like chat. And the red dot nags me.
first_pass.solution: Label it 'More' and only show the red dot when something really needs me.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing it shows what is behind it and what the red dot was about
test_cases.action: Press the purple three-dot circle at the right of the bottom row. Read what appears. Press the phone's Back button to close it, then the house.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears is not what you expected, or the red dot is still unexplained
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears is a short list you expected
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the purple three-dot circle. A small sheet slid up with two items: Profile and Video Call, each with its own red dot. I pressed Back: the page behind switched to Home, but the sheet stayed open. A second Back did nothing. Pressing the house finally closed it.

screen1-a20.closing_comment: A short 'more' list, which is what I expected. But the red dots just moved onto Profile and Video Call with no reason given, and Back wouldn't close the sheet. I had to find another way out, which is exactly how I lose my thread.

screen34-a7.cue: The words themselves, right under 'Your Spanish Score is 1'.

screen34-a8.expectation: Starts or opens a maths course.

first_pass.why: Labelled.

screen34-a9.where: New Courses row: purple music-note tile with Music
screen34-a9.expectation: Starts or opens a music course.

first_pass.why: Labelled.

screen34-a10.expectation: Starts or opens a chess course.

first_pass.why: Labelled.

screen34-a11.expectation: Tapping the dark area closes the panel and brings me back.

test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: pressing the grey area closed the panel as you expected

screen34-a11.closing_comment: Pressing the grey area closed it just as I'd guessed. I'd still like a visible X for my first time, but it works the way I expected.

screen35-a1.where: top row, far left: little Spanish flag with a 1

test_cases.targets: whether pressing it shows what it is for and what the number means

test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens does not make plain what the flag was for, or still leaves the number unexplained
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens plainly shows what the flag is for and what the number counts
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the flag at the top left. A panel dropped down showing my Spanish course with a blue outline, a '+ Course' tile, a bar from 1 to 2 and 'Your Spanish Score is 1' with MORE ABOUT SCORE. Then New Courses: Math, Music, Chess. Back closed it.

screen35-a1.closing_comment: The flag is 'my course', and the panel spells out that the 1 is my Spanish Score. One tap and I understood both, and I'd remember it.

screen35-a2.where: top row, second: grey flame with a 1
screen35-a2.expectation: Shows my streak - how many days in a row I've practised.
screen35-a2.cue: The flame. Every habit app uses a flame for a streak.

screen35-a3.where: top row, middle: blue gem with 520

screen35-a3.cue: The gem picture and the big number.

screen35-a4.where: top row, right: pink lightning bolt with 25

screen35-a4.cue: The lightning bolt looks like a battery / energy.

first_pass.why: I get 'energy' from the bolt, but I have no idea what uses it or what 25 means until I tap it.
first_pass.solution: A short word like 'Energy' next to it, or a 25/25 so I can see it's a full tank.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing it shows it is an app thing (not the phone battery) and what the number is
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the pink bolt-and-battery at the top-right. Read what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens still leaves you unsure what it is or what the number means
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens makes plain what it is and what the number means

screen35-a4.closing_comment: It's clearly the app's energy, not my phone battery, and 25/25 tells me I'm full. What it still never says is what uses the energy up, so I only half understand it.

screen35-a5.where: big green banner: SECTION 1, UNIT 1 - Order at a cafe

first_pass.why: The words say where I am, great, but it looks like a heading, not a button. I wouldn't know tapping it does anything.

test_cases.targets: whether you can tell it can be pressed, and whether pressing it does what you expected
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the words on the green bar at the top (not the small notebook at its right end). See what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: nothing on the bar told you it could be pressed, or what opened was not what you expected from the words
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opened is what you expected from the words on the bar

screen35-a5.closing_comment: What opened (a map of the whole course) is roughly what I'd expect from a 'Section 1, Unit 1' banner. But nothing on the bar itself told me it was a button; I only found out by poking it.

screen35-a6.where: right end of the green banner: white notebook-with-lines icon
screen35-a6.expectation: Opens notes or a guidebook for this unit - tips and key phrases.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the notebook settles which of your guesses it is
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the small notebook at the right end of the green bar. Read what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is not what you guessed, or still does not tell you what the notebook stands for
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens matches one of your guesses and you would remember it next time
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the small notebook on the right of the green bar. A page opened with the owl, 'SECTION 1, UNIT 1 - Order at a café' and KEY PHRASES: Spanish sentences with English under each and a speaker icon to hear them. I closed it with the X.

screen35-a6.closing_comment: It's the guide with key phrases for the unit, exactly one of my guesses, and I'd remember it next time. I'd still like the word 'Guide' under it, but it didn't trip me.

screen35-a7.expectation: No idea - some promotion or event with another game? The red ! makes me feel I have to press it.
screen35-a7.cue: The skull badge (looks like a game logo) and the red exclamation mark.

first_pass.why: It's a mash of owl, skull logo and a red alarm dot with no words. It grabs my eye away from my lesson and doesn't tell me what it is.
first_pass.solution: Tell me in words what it is ('Brawl Stars event') and lose the alarm dot unless something is actually urgent.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the badge tells you what it is and what the red mark was about
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the cartoon owl-and-skull picture at the left, under the green bar. Read what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left, or the lower blue text button if there is no X. Do NOT press any button that says it claims on or opens another game.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens still does not make plain what this is, or it takes you somewhere you could not have predicted
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens makes plain what it is and you could predict it next time

I pressed CLAIM LATER, which then opened a second page, 'Brawl Stars Quest - INCOMPLETE', with a Day 1 to Day 7 list of rewards. I closed that with the X. Back on the path, the red ! had gone.

screen35-a7.closing_comment: Now I know it's a 7-day tie-in with another game, and the red ! meant a reward waiting. But 'Chaos Drops' means nothing to me, CLAIM LATER sent me into another page I didn't expect, and the whole thing pulled me away from my lesson for two screens.

screen35-a8.where: top of the winding path: round green button with a white star in a green ring
screen35-a8.cue: It's the one bright green button on the path, with a ring around it - that's 'you are here'.

first_pass.why: The colour and ring make it the obvious next step. Exactly what I want: one clear thing to press.

screen35-a9.where: purple pill under the owl: '13 days'
screen35-a9.expectation: Shows how long an event lasts or how many days are left; tapping probably opens the same thing as the owl badge.

first_pass.why: 13 days of what? Left? Done? It's a number with no subject.
first_pass.solution: Say '13 days left' plus what it's for.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the pill tells you what the time count refers to
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the purple pill under the owl-and-skull picture. Read what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens does not tell you what the days referred to
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens says plainly what the days count
test_cases.what_happened: On my phone the purple pill said 'Ended', not a number of days. I pressed it and got the same 'Brawl Stars Quest - INCOMPLETE' page with Day 1 to Day 7. I closed it with the X.

screen35-a9.closing_comment: The pill says 'Ended' while the page says 'Incomplete' and talks about days 1 to 7. Nothing tells me what the day count on the pill was counting or what has ended. I'm more confused, not less.

screen35-a11.where: path, second button: round grey star button
screen35-a11.expectation: A lesson I haven't unlocked yet - pressing probably tells me it's locked.
screen35-a11.cue: It's grey, like the others further down, and the green one is above it.

first_pass.why: Grey means 'not yet' - I get it from the path order.

screen35-a12.where: path, grey star button on the left
screen35-a12.expectation: Same as the other grey star - a later lesson, locked for now.

Same as the other grey stars.

first_pass.why: There's no word and the picture doesn't mean anything to me. I'd have to tap it just to find out, and then I'd lose my place.
first_pass.solution: Put a word under every bottom button, like most apps do.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the bird makes plain what it is for

test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is not something you could have guessed from the bird
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens is what you expected and you would recognise the bird next time

screen35-a15.closing_comment: A bird that opens a paid-plans page. I could never have guessed that, and it sits in the main menu next to Home like any other part of the app. Now I know, I'd avoid it.

screen35-a16.where: bottom row, far left: little house (highlighted blue)
screen35-a16.expectation: Home - takes me to this main learning path.

first_pass.why: House is home, everywhere.

screen35-a17.where: bottom row, second: orange square frame with a keyhole in the middle
screen35-a17.expectation: Maybe rewards or a treasure box? Not sure.

first_pass.solution: A word under it.

test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens matches what the chest led you to expect

screen35-a17.closing_comment: Close to my 'rewards' guess, since the chests are prizes, but I'd never have come up with 'Quests'. I'll remember it now, though.

screen35-a18.where: bottom row, third: brown cup / trophy

first_pass.why: Trophy is either rankings or badges - I'd guess, not know.
first_pass.solution: A word under it.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing it settles which of your readings is right
test_cases.action: Press the cup/trophy shape in the bottom row. Read what opens. Then press the house.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is not what you expected, or you still could not tell which it would be next time
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens matches what you expected
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the brown cup. A page opened with a 1-2-3 ranking picture and 'Finish 2 lessons to start competing on Leaderboards!'.

screen35-a18.closing_comment: Leaderboard was my first guess, and the page confirmed it straight away.

screen35-a19.where: bottom row, fourth: pink speech bubble with a heart

first_pass.why: Heart plus bubble could be messages, favourites or a friends feed. Too many options.
first_pass.solution: A word under it.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing it settles which of your readings is right
test_cases.action: Press the heart-in-a-bubble in the bottom row. Read what opens. Then press the house.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is none of the things you guessed, or you could not tell which in advance
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens is what you expected
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the pink heart-in-a-bubble. A 'Feed' page opened with empty friend circles, 'Start Friend Streaks to send and receive daily gifts!', ADD FRIENDS, and a post from someone who 'shared a sentence'. Then I went to the chest (next try).

screen35-a19.closing_comment: It's the friends feed, one of my three guesses, so it wasn't a shock. But I couldn't have picked which one in advance. A word under it would settle it.

screen35-a20.expectation: More options / everything else, or maybe chat. The red dot says something new is waiting.

first_pass.why: Three dots is 'more', OK, but in a speech bubble it also looks like chat. And the red dot nags me.
first_pass.solution: Label it 'More' and only show the red dot when something really needs me.

test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears is a short list you expected

screen35-a20.closing_comment: A short 'more' list, which is what I expected. But the red dots just moved onto Profile and Video Call with no reason given, and Back wouldn't close the sheet. I had to find another way out, which is exactly how I lose my thread.
